mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over the same month signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with falling inflation, which may trigger risk-off behavior and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive months signals a precautionary savings behavior, which depresses demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises AND GDPC1 falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above trend by more than 1% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as earnings growth compensates.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS above trend by >1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) for six consecutive months signals a recovery in residential construction activity, which boosts demand for materials and labor and supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises month-over-month for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
